families._definition: having characteristics that attract love or affection

members.tone: The family's plain baseline - it says the thing has whatever draws love, without dressing the quality up as innocence or sweetness.
members._gloss: having characteristics that attract love or affection

members.tone: The full-spelt form, identical in warmth and force to *lovable*.
members._gloss: having characteristics that attract love or affection

members.tone: Superlative where *lovable* is merely descriptive - affection is not attracted but compelled, and the childlike or naive streak is what compels it.
members._gloss: lovable especially in a childlike or naive way

members.tone: Puts the effect in motion rather than the quality at rest: it wins affection over, where *adorable* simply announces the winning is done.
members._gloss: lovable especially in a childlike or naive way

members.tone: Broad, easy warmth for the same childlike appeal, without the surrender *adorable* implies.
members._gloss: lovable especially in a childlike or naive way

members.tone: Lifts sweetness to an ideal - praise that leaves no room for a fault in the nature described.
members._gloss: having a sweet nature befitting an angel or cherub

members.tone: The extended form of *angelic*, reaching for the same unblemished sweetness with a more formal ring.
members._gloss: having a sweet nature befitting an angel or cherub

members.tone: Takes the cherub rather than the angel: sweetness that is small, round and fond instead of exalted.
members._gloss: having a sweet nature befitting an angel or cherub

members.tone: The most rarefied of the angel words - sweetness raised to something radiant and remote, well past the homely warmth of *cherubic*.
members._gloss: having a sweet nature befitting an angel or cherub

members.tone: The unadorned name for the nature the angel words put wings on - the same quality with none of the exaltation.
members._gloss: having a sweet nature befitting an angel or cherub

members.tone: Carries the invitation in its build - a thing that asks to be held, stated more deliberately than *cuddly*.
Soft, offhand and physical: the appeal is being huggable, not being good-natured as in *sweet*.

families.axis: plainly suitable → propriety pushed past its purpose
families._definition: marked by suitability or rightness or appropriateness

members.tone: The plain baseline of the family - approves a thing as suitable, right or appropriate without naming the standard it is measured by.
members._gloss: marked by suitability or rightness or appropriateness

members.tone: Warm approval - what accords with custom is credited with grace rather than mere compliance, unlike the dry *decorous*.
Gentle and pleased - it finds conduct agreeable in its accord with propriety rather than measuring it against a rule.
A phrase rather than a word, and formal to the point of ceremony - approval delivered by invoking the code instead of describing the conduct.
Cool and external - conduct is held up against a standard of propriety and passes, with none of the warmth of *becoming*.
Understated - grants that conduct accords with propriety without the ceremony *decorous* brings to the same verdict.
Approval as a verdict - the social rule was met, and nothing warmer than that is claimed.
The bluntest way to render the same social judgement as *correct*, carrying no formality at all.
Approval keyed to the occasion and the people in it rather than to any code - it praises harmony where *correct* praises compliance.
members._gloss: in harmony with the spirit of particular persons or occasion

members.tone: Modest and human - it grants that a thing suits the persons and the moment, with less deliberation than *fitting*.
members._gloss: in harmony with the spirit of particular persons or occasion

members.tone: A designation rather than a compliment - it states that something is proper or legitimate under a named law, and the approval belongs to that law and not to the speaker.
members._gloss: proper or legitimate according to Muslim law
members._note_5_3: screen flagged religion; kept - the gloss is a dietary-law fact, not a judgement of a faith. The author may withhold.

members.tone: Informal and reassuring - declares a thing proper or legitimate, above board and open to no objection.
Contemptuous - the excess of propriety is read as self-satisfaction, correctness worn as superiority over others.
The lightest fault in this group - propriety held so tightly it stiffens, mocked rather than condemned.
Dismissive and faintly ridiculing - the overdone propriety is treated as fussiness, silly rather than severe like *priggish*.
Propriety inflated into squeamishness - more disapproving than *prim*, since the excess is taken as a readiness to be shocked.

families.axis: dismissed as worthless or half-pitied → contemptible in the most absolute degree

members.tone: The family's plain verdict: it states that scorn is deserved without supplying any of the scorn itself, where *scummy* supplies nothing else.
Formal and absolute, it puts the thing at the very floor of the scale with none of *low-down*'s sneer.
One blunt syllable for the bottom of the scale, carrying the direction of the fall and nothing more.
Informal, and the trailing particle adds a drawled contempt that flat *low* leaves out.
Contempt with wretchedness folded into it, so the thing comes off squalid as well as low.
The most physically disgusted of these, treating the utterly contemptible as filth you would rather not touch.
Comes out as a curse rather than an assessment, the contempt thrown instead of delivered.

members._skip_reason: 5.3: birth-status slur, same class as the held family illegitimate - pre-skipped by the session; the author may clear it

members.tone: Writes a thing off as amounting to nothing, a dismissal by worthlessness rather than the earned scorn of *contemptible*.
Contempt leads and pity trails: the scorn is the louder half of the mixture.
The gentler face of the same mixed response, letting the pity carry the weight the contempt in *pathetic* takes.
Holds both halves at once, asking you to feel sorry for the thing and look down on it in the same breath.

families.axis: merely liable to sin → wicked past any reform
families._definition: morally bad in principle or practice

members.tone: The plain, unhedged moral verdict, and it covers both the settled principle and the actual practice rather than choosing between them.
members._gloss: morally bad in principle or practice

members.tone: Names the thing as vice itself rather than describing a fault in it, which makes it absolute where *wicked* is merely damning.
Presents vice as the settled bent of the thing, so it sounds like a diagnosis of character beside *evil*'s flat sentence.
A casting word: it marks the villain's part, or the actor filling it, and condemns nobody.
members._gloss: (of an actor or role) being or playing the villain

members.tone: Formal and heavy-syllabled, delivering the same extreme-and-criminal verdict as *heinous* in a more elevated register.
The blunt public condemnation, wickedness pitched so far into the criminal that the word works almost as a sentence.
The gravest of its group, weighing the wrong as an enormity rather than simply logging it as sin like *sinful*.
members._gloss: characterized by iniquity; wicked because it is believed to be a sin

members.tone: The plainest naming of wickedness-as-sin, condemnatory without the swell of *iniquitous*.
members._gloss: characterized by iniquity; wicked because it is believed to be a sin

members.tone: Measures the wickedness as distance from godliness, so the fault is a standing away rather than *sinful*'s committed offence.
members._gloss: characterized by iniquity; wicked because it is believed to be a sin

members.tone: Pictures reform as recovery and denies it — nothing here can be got back.
The heaviest of these four, since redemption is what it withholds: a final verdict rather than a prognosis.
The same refusal built on a blunt negative prefix, more workaday in sound than *irredeemable*.
The flattest of the group, stating only that reform will not take, with none of *irredeemable*'s note of lost salvation.
Condemns the wickedness in the abstract, where *villainous* points instead at the one committing it.
Casts the extreme wickedness as a villain's, making it a fact of character rather than of the deed.
The mildest here by a wide margin: it concedes only that sin is possible, not that any has been done.

families.axis: a passing freshening → the imparting of life itself

members.tone: The plain, full-strength word for the effect, and the only one here that promises strength as well as liveliness, where *enlivening* offers spirit alone.
Warm approval aimed at spirit rather than muscle - what it gives is vivacity, not the strength *invigorating* claims.
The same gift of spirit as *animating*, but framed as a lift applied to something that was flat before.
Approval with a bite in it - the energy arrives sharply, where *refreshing* delivers the same energy gently.
Mild and matter-of-fact praise that renders vitality as pace and snap rather than as depth of force.
The simplest word in the group for this energy, crediting clarity and cleanness with the lift that *bracing* wins by sharpness.
Easy, grateful approval - the energy it names reads as relief from tiredness rather than as a charge of power.
Identical in force to *refreshing* but stiffer in build, which lends the same lift a formal weight.
Cool, measured approval that credits a thing with steadying and energizing rather than delighting, unlike the showier *exhilarating*.

members._gloss: used of a medicine that is strengthening
members._skip_reason: gloss is a usage restriction, not a definition

members.tone: The high end of the family - the lift goes past energy into open cheerfulness, which *stimulating* stops short of.
Cooler than *exhilarating* for the same effect, naming the rousing of liveliness and good cheer without saying how high it rises.
The most absolute claim available here, since what it grants is life and spirit outright rather than a boost to either.
members._gloss: giving or having the power to give life and spirit

members.tone: The same gift of life and spirit as *life-giving*, stated as a working effect rather than as the grand attribute.
members._gloss: giving or having the power to give life and spirit

members.tone: Approval for a lift that is a return of something lost - new life and vigor given back, not given for the first time as in *life-giving*.
members._gloss: tending to impart new life and vigor to

members.tone: Names the same power of return as a settled property of the thing, calmer and more formal than the active *renewing*.
members._gloss: tending to impart new life and vigor to

families.axis: plain vitality → spirits fizzing over into speech

members.tone: The plain measure of the family — life and energy stated without a metaphor attached, so every other member here is a way of colouring it.
Credits life and spirit rather than motion, and leans on a following 'with' to name whatever the thing is brimming over with.
members._gloss: (often followed by ‘with’) full of life and spirit

members.tone: Liveliness as vigorous springing action — sturdier and more robust than *bouncy*, which makes the same spring sound weightless.
The spring taken as a temperament rather than a feat — lighter and more playful than *bouncing*.
Informal and brisk — lively action as a snap of energy, with none of the dignity *spirited* carries.
The dignified member: lively action with mettle and will behind it, where *peppy* is only pep.
Informal, and here the lively action is speed — quickness rather than the buoyancy of *bouncy*.
Puts freshness beside the animation, so the liveliness comes across as light and easy where *spirited* comes across as strong.
Covers both being full of high spirits and showing them, naming the outward fizz and the inward supply at once.
members._gloss: full of or showing high spirits

members.tone: High spirits or excitement caught in the act of rising — a thing in motion where *bubbly* names a settled quality.
members._gloss: marked by high spirits or excitement

members.tone: The polished word for the same fizz — high spirits or excitement described with a formality the shorter members refuse.
members._gloss: marked by high spirits or excitement

members.tone: The weakest approval of the fizz: the high spirits or excitement are granted, but froth lets them look light and easily dispersed.
members._gloss: marked by high spirits or excitement

members.tone: The brightest of the set — high spirits or excitement that flash and dazzle rather than merely bubble.
members._gloss: marked by high spirits or excitement

members.tone: The same flash in a smaller, prettier register — decorative where *scintillating* is dazzling.
members._gloss: marked by high spirits or excitement

members.tone: Moves the fizz into the voice: enthusiasm uttered with nothing holding it back, warm but with an ear on the overflow.
Names the quality of that unrestrained enthusiasm rather than a burst of it — looser and more casual than *burbling*.

_purpose: Census 012 control arm. Six gate-eligible, unauthored adjective families drawn from data/worklist.tsv, authored in the same tick as draft-018 with the same unchanged instruments, so the candidate draw (71% noun) has a stratum directly comparable to censuses 007-010 (100% adjective). The 5% stop condition applies per stratum, never to the blend. Pre-registered before any read: data/policy/census-012.json.
